text: Fixed a scoring bug. The flip was graded as a ceiling even on days SPY was already above it, so ordinary days got logged as misses. We also stopped giving the map a free point every day the market didn't whipsaw.
Levels are now graded on where SPY closes, not the intraday wick. Dealers sell rallies into these levels, so price often pokes through and closes back under. That is the level working, not failing.
The put wall is no longer graded as support. The map has always called it a crowd, not a floor, so scoring it as a floor was grading a claim we never made.
The upside line now leads with the brake instead of the flip. Over the first 10 days the brakes held on the close every time they were tested. The flip held half the time.

Every accuracy number now comes with a comparison: plain $5 round numbers, graded the same way on the same days. If the map can't beat round numbers, you'll see it. Because the rules changed, the track record restarts today.

The tally line now says how long the map has been running (every night since Sep 23) and that its record restarted Oct 8 when the grading was fixed. It used to just count from the restart, which made it look like day one.

The ELSE road ('it holds between X and Y') is now the gap between the two IF levels, so the three roads cover every price. It used to be drawn off the pin and the gamma flip, and tonight that would have read 'holds between 776 and 777' while SPY sat at 778.10: the do-nothing branch did not contain the current price.

Fixed the 'if it goes down' line. When the book had no real support just under the price, the map fell back to rounding the price down, so tonight it would have read 'IF it goes below 778' with SPY sitting at 778.01: a down-branch that fires on a one-cent move, and a do-nothing range that barely contained the current price. The down trigger is now the first actual level below the price that the map names, so tonight it reads 'below 775' and the quiet range is 775 to 780. Nothing about the grading changed.

The 'quiet range' road no longer swings further than its own box. It wobbles around the pin, and the pin is usually off-centre in the range, so on a wide range it was drawn poking above the ceiling it was supposed to be stuck under. It is now capped to stay inside the band, which is what a drift should look like.

Fixed the mirror of last night's bug, on the 'if it goes up' line. The up road leads with the first heavy level above the price that dealers defend, but when the book has no such level at all, the line had nothing to name: it read 'IF it goes higher' with no number, and the quiet range collapsed to a penny above the current price. It now falls back to the next thing the road does name, and it no longer claims dealers are braking when there is no level above the price for them to brake at. Tonight's book was one missing strike away from printing that, so it got fixed before it shipped. Grading is untouched.

Two label fixes on the chart itself. The note on the right-hand end of each road is a full sentence, but the space reserved for it was a fixed width, so a long one ran off the edge of the picture: tonight the up road read "dealers buy into stre" with the rest of the word outside the image. That gutter is now measured from the text that is actually going to be drawn in it. And the small "beyond a typical day" line that marks how far SPY usually travels was printed on whatever row it landed on, so tonight it was written straight through the flip label and both sentences turned to mush. It now checks the row first and steps below the line if it is taken. Nothing about the levels or the grading changed.
